incidents.vector: Poisoned Visual Studio Code extension compromised an employee endpoint, giving attackers access to roughly 3,800 internal GitHub source-code repositories.
incidents.impact: GitHub confirmed exfiltration of internal repositories and rotated critical secrets. The TeamPCP group advertised the stolen code for $50,000 on a cybercrime forum; GitHub says no customer data was affected and the incident remains under investigation.

incidents.vector: Theft of franchisee documents from a corporate document-storage system, part of the broader ShinyHunters Salesforce data-theft wave.
incidents.impact: 7-Eleven confirmed names, addresses, and Social Security numbers of franchisee personnel were stolen. The breach was reported to state regulators in Maine, Vermont, and Massachusetts; the total number of affected individuals was not disclosed.

incidents.victim: Cybercrime ecosystem (Microsoft disruption of Fox Tempest)
incidents.vector: Fox Tempest operated a malware-signing-as-a-service that abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to issue more than 1,000 fraudulent code-signing certificates to ransomware affiliates.
incidents.impact: Microsoft seized the operation's website (signspace[.]cloud), took hundreds of VMs offline, and revoked the certificates. The service had enabled Rhysida, INC, Qilin, Akira, and other ransomware deployments globally — including prior attacks on the British Library and Seattle-Tacoma airport.

incidents.vector: Public disclosure of three new Windows zero-days (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma) plus a working PoC for a 2020 flaw Microsoft thought was patched, released without coordinated disclosure.
incidents.impact: YellowKey bypasses BitLocker via a malicious USB; GreenPlasma escalates to SYSTEM; MiniPlasma exploits CVE-2020-17103 on fully patched Windows 11. BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) from the same researcher is already in CISA's KEV. Most flaws remain unpatched.

incidents.victim: CISA / U.S. Department of Homeland Security
incidents.attacker: Unknown — credentials exposed by contractor mistake
incidents.vector: A Nightwing contractor maintained a public GitHub repository ("Private-CISA") for roughly six months that exposed plaintext credentials to three AWS GovCloud accounts and dozens of internal CISA systems, including the agency's DevSecOps landing zone.
incidents.impact: Researchers validated the AWS keys were still active. CISA says it has no evidence sensitive data was accessed; Senator Maggie Hassan has demanded a classified briefing. The exposed keys remained valid for 48 hours after notification.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of an unpatched cross-site scripting zero-day (CVE-2026-42897) in Outlook Web Access; a specially crafted email triggers arbitrary JavaScript when opened.
incidents.impact: Successful exploitation gives attackers access to victim mailboxes and session tokens, enabling email theft, forwarding-rule persistence, and follow-on business email compromise. CISA added the flaw to KEV; Microsoft has issued only mitigations, no patch.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-exposed automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems lacking password protection at U.S. gas stations.
incidents.impact: Attackers altered displayed fuel-level readings but did not change actual fuel quantities. CNN reported the activity; no significant operational impact yet, but officials view it as Iran's strategic signaling amid the ongoing US/Israel-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure.

incidents.victim: Unnamed enterprise (Storm-2949 victim, Microsoft IR case)
incidents.vector: Social engineering of Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) for Entra ID combined with MFA-prompt manipulation, followed by abuse of legitimate Azure RBAC and management APIs (App Service publishing profiles, Key Vault) to pivot across the cloud estate.
incidents.impact: The threat actor compromised multiple identities, exfiltrated large volumes of files from SharePoint/OneDrive, and pivoted into Azure App Service, Key Vaults, and Storage accounts. Operation relied solely on legitimate cloud features rather than malware to evade detection.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (CoinbaseCartel / SLSH affiliate)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized party obtained a token with access to Grafana Labs' GitHub environment and downloaded the company codebase.
incidents.impact: Grafana confirmed the codebase was stolen but found no evidence of customer data or production system access. The company refused to pay the ransom, invalidated compromised credentials, and is preparing for possible public release of the code.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia, and UK (BlackFile campaign)
incidents.vector: High-volume voice phishing (vishing) calls to employees' personal phones, combined with real-time adversary-in-the-middle MFA capture, leading to Microsoft 365/Okta SSO compromise and scripted exfiltration from SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce, and Zendesk via Microsoft Graph and python-requests.
incidents.impact: Mandiant/GTIG attributes dozens of recent intrusions since early 2026. In one case the actor downloaded over a million files from a single victim. Operators pressure non-paying victims with Gmail spam floods, voicemail threats to executives, and swatting.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of malicious Ruby packages published on May 11-12 attempted cross-site scripting and data theft specifically targeting RubyGems engineers and staff.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled all new user sign-ups after the attack. Maintainers said the team "has been on this for hours"; what data was stolen remains unclear. Incident is unrelated to the concurrent TanStack npm worm.

incidents.victim: TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenSearch and ~170 npm/PyPI packages
incidents.vector: GitHub Actions pull_request_target workflow abuse and cache poisoning on the TanStack repo allowed attackers to extract the OIDC token from a privileged runner and publish poisoned versions through TanStack's legitimate release pipeline.
incidents.impact: The self-spreading Mini Shai-Hulud worm poisoned 42 @tanstack packages in six minutes (@tanstack/react-router has ~12M weekly downloads) and propagated to ~170 npm/PyPI packages with cumulative downloads above 500M. First documented npm attack shipping with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance. Includes a 1-in-6 destructive wipe payload on Israeli/Iranian-locale hosts. Source code was leaked publicly on May 14.

incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas (~275M students and faculty, ~9,000 institutions)
incidents.vector: Initial access via compromised "Free-For-Teacher" accounts with excessive standing privileges, followed by rapid lateral movement and mass exfiltration of ~3.65 TB of data.
incidents.impact: Attackers defaced Canvas login pages at hundreds of schools during final-exams week and forced the platform offline. Instructure paid an undisclosed ransom; Canvas was restored over the weekend. Congress opened an investigation and the FBI issued a ShinyHunters-specific advisory.

incidents.vector: Trojanized version of the Checkmarx Jenkins AST scanner plugin (2026.5.09) was published to the Jenkins Marketplace.
incidents.impact: The malicious plugin was installed by several hundred Jenkins controllers during the May 9-10 exposure window. This is the third compromise of Checkmarx by the same supply chain crew in three months. Remediated builds were published the same day.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools users (AVB Disc Soft); targeted government, research, manufacturing and retail orgs in Russia, Belarus, Thailand
incidents.vector: Supply chain compromise of the DAEMON Tools website; installers signed with the legitimate vendor certificate have shipped with a first-stage backdoor since at least April 8.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky observed thousands of infections, but the second-stage QUIC RAT was deployed to only about a dozen high-value targets across government, research, manufacturing, and retail in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand. Tradecraft mirrors prior Chinese-actor compromises of Notepad++ and CCleaner.

incidents.vector: Maliciously crafted network traffic exploited a previously undocumented zero-day in Huawei enterprise routers, sending them into a continuous restart loop.
incidents.impact: POST's landline, 4G, and 5G networks went down for more than three hours, cutting off emergency-services access for potentially hundreds of thousands of residents. Investigators concluded POST was not specifically targeted. Ten months later no CVE has been issued and Huawei has not publicly disclosed the flaw.
